newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term rates rise as tightness persists.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term rates rise as tightness persists.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates rose across the board due to a persistent liquidity crunch and the presence of finance companies and merchant banks, which are considered higher risk borrowers in Malaysia, dealers said.
They said one-week money was at 7.70 percent against 7.30/40, two-week at 7.70 against 7.20/25 and one-month at 7.35 against 7.20/25.
Three-month money at 7.25/30 percent and six-month 7.30 were both unchanged from their previous levels.
"There is no fresh reason. It is just that there are some bad names in the market and no fresh liquidity is coming in," said the head of money market dealing at a local bank.
He said the market was extremely quiet, with the perpetually short finance companies being the main borrowers in the market.
Dealers said the overnight remaining high at 8.7 percent had also affected sentiment for short-term rates.
But, they said a maturity of a Bank Negara bill on Friday could ease the situation. - Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
